t: Hungary's change from communism to capitalism, the rendszerváltás, was peaceful: Round Table Talks began in March 1989, Imre Nagy was reburied as a martyr that June, and free elections in May 1990 made József Antall prime minister.
Hungary joined NATO in 1999, the European Union on 1 May 2004 and the Schengen Area in 2007; in January 2008 its border guards were merged into the police.

From 2010 Viktor Orbán's Fidesz won four parliamentary supermajorities and passed a new constitution, in an era of democratic backsliding that ended when Péter Magyar's Tisza Party won the election of April 2026.
dyk: Hungary's Fundamental Law contains eternity clauses guaranteeing human dignity, the separation of powers, the state structure and the rule of law, which even the two-thirds supermajority needed for other amendments may not touch.
ev: The Hungarian Socialist Workers' Party opens Round Table Talks with the opposition in March; the reburial of Imre Nagy in June marks the symbolic end of communism in Hungary.
Free elections in May bring the Hungarian Democratic Forum to the head of a coalition; József Antall becomes the first democratically elected prime minister since the Second World War.
The removal of state subsidies and rapid privatisation, with the Yugoslav Wars on the southern border, bring a severe recession.
Hungary joins the European Union on 1 May.
Viktor Orbán's Fidesz wins a two-thirds parliamentary supermajority and the legislature approves a new constitution.
Péter Magyar's Tisza Party wins a supermajority in the election of 12 April; Magyar is sworn in as prime minister on 9 May.

f.predecessor: Hungarian People's Republic (1949–1989), a Soviet satellite state in the Warsaw Pact
